The 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee, reported meniscus injury). Christian McCaffrey has been cleared to play. 3286.take: If he's activated, he's one of the most experienced healthy receivers on a depleted 49ers roster, which could mean a lot of routes right away. He's coming off a five-game absence and has never been a high-volume target, so treat him as a deep-league flex dart in a decent matchup, not a lineup lock. Confirm his activation before Sunday's late games. In dynasty, he's a veteran with only short-term value, so a rebuilding team should sell if he produces.

6803.name: Brandon Aiyuk
6803.headline: Reinstatement filed; release, not a trade, looks more likely
6803.news: Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus and filed for reinstatement on Nov. 4. Rosenhaus said he planned to report to the 49ers' facility on Friday, Nov. 6. Because he applied before the Nov. 10 deadline, San Francisco can't deny the request. Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch have repeatedly said he won't play for the team again, and reports say any trade or release would come only after he reports. ESPN says Washington hasn't completely dropped trade interest, but most coverage calls a release the likeliest result; that would push roughly $21.2 million in remaining payments onto the 2026-27 cap. Reports also note that a failed physical could land him on IR. He has not played this season.
6803.take: The situation is moving toward a resolution, but release looks more likely than a deadline trade, and even then he would need to sign somewhere and get into game shape. Don't expect real redraft value before late December. In dynasty his price is as low as it gets, so a rebuilder should hold and see where he lands for 2027, or buy him almost for free if another manager has given up.

6819.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
6819.headline: On IR with foot injury; Week 10 is the earliest return
6819.news: Pittsburgh put Pittman on short-term injured reserve after he aggravated a foot injury in practice that was later described as plantar fasciitis, and Mike McCarthy said he would miss multiple weeks. He didn't play in Week 8, and the Steelers are on bye in Week 9, so the Nov. 15 game against Cincinnati in Week 10 is his earliest return. A ClutchPoints report says he has been running on his own and is aiming to return after the bye, but he has not been designated to return. The foot has bothered him all season: he missed Week 2 and caught 2 of 5 targets for 16 yards in his Week 3 return. One tracker had him at 7 catches for 89 yards and no touchdowns in three games.
6819.take: He was a low-volume WR4 when he did play, and in his absence rookie Germie Bernard has settled in as the WR2 behind DK Metcalf. Plantar fasciitis tends to linger, so even if he returns in Week 10 he may not take back a full role right away. In redraft, keep him in an IR slot if one is open; otherwise he's a drop in 12-team leagues. In dynasty he's an aging veteran with an injury, so a rebuilding team has nothing to buy, and his trade value is too low to sell until he shows he's healthy.

12506.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
12506.headline: Career-best 10-154 in Week 8; Shedeur Sanders starts at New Orleans
12506.news: Fannin caught 10 of 12 targets for a career-high 154 yards, and lost a fumble, in the Browns' 27-6 loss at Pittsburgh in Week 8. Most of that came in a blowout with Deshaun Watson throwing 39 times. Across his last two games he has 16 catches for 245 yards. Todd Monken announced Friday, Nov. 6, that Shedeur Sanders will start Sunday at New Orleans because Watson (concussion protocol, questionable) has missed too much practice. Fannin had a minor groin issue during the week, but Monken said he's just sore and will play, and he is off the injury report. Previews note the Saints allow the sixth-most fantasy points to tight ends.
12506.take: His target share is at a TE1 level and the matchup is good, so he's a start even with the QB change. Sanders adds some volatility, but the two connected on a long touchdown as rookies last year, and a young quarterback tends to lean on his tight end. The 154 yards came in garbage time, so expect regression, but he's a top-8 TE for Week 9. In dynasty he's a 22-year-old ascending tight end, exactly the kind of asset a rebuilding team should keep, and we wouldn't sell after one big game unless the offer is a premium one.

2306.name: Jameis Winston
2306.headline: Relieves injured McCarthy; likely Thursday starter vs. Washington
2306.news: Winston came on in relief of J.J. McCarthy (hip) on Nov. 8 and went 6-of-8 for 71 yards and a touchdown. If McCarthy can't go on a short week, Winston is the likely starter Thursday against Washington. He opened the season as the Giants' starter after Jaxson Dart's season-ending knee injury, then lost the job to McCarthy, whom New York acquired from Minnesota in late September. We could not find a Giants update on how serious McCarthy's hip injury is.
2306.take: Winston's appeal is volume: he throws aggressively, and that produces yards and touchdowns along with interceptions. A Thursday start against Washington makes him a usable streamer in superflex and a low-end QB2 in 12-team 1QB leagues, but only if McCarthy is ruled out. He's a short-term bridge on a losing team, so there's no long-term dynasty value. A 1-6 rebuilding team can pick him up for spot starts, but he shouldn't cost anything in a trade.

8161.name: Malik Willis
8161.headline: Groin limits Willis in 19-9 loss to Detroit
8161.news: Willis was clearly limited by a groin injury in Miami's 19-9 loss to Detroit on Nov. 8, finishing 13-of-25 for 128 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. Afterward he said the groin 'was tight,' and he is listed as questionable going forward. He had managed the groin all week, logging a full practice on Oct. 28 and appearing on the Week 9 injury report on Nov. 5. Some outlets had called him a streaming option against the Lions before the game.
8161.take: He was a streamer because of his rushing, and a groin injury cuts into exactly that. Without the legs, his passing alone doesn't hold up in fantasy, as this week's line shows. Sit him in 12-team 1QB leagues until he practices fully again. In superflex dynasty he's a bridge starter with a low ceiling; hold him as QB depth, but he won't bring a return a rebuilding team cares about.

Watch Wednesday's practice report for Henderson's status and any Stevenson diagnosis before setting Week 10 lineups. In redraft, hold him and start him as an RB2/flex if he practices fully and Stevenson is out. In dynasty, he's the kind of young, explosive back a rebuilding team should be holding onto, not selling during a short illness absence.

One cited projection has him at about 40 yards, and FantasyPros points to a high aDOT and big air-yard totals. We didn't find any current injury designation.
9756.take: More slot work should steady a player whose weekly results have swung widely, and deep targets give him a ceiling in any matchup. For tonight, treat him as a WR3/flex with boom-or-bust risk instead of a locked-in starter. In dynasty he's a young starter, and the rising usage argues against selling at what looks like a fair price, so hold. Consider selling only if a contender pays based on a big MNF game.
